task.prompt: Implement one independent source-only task: propose complete TypeScript for packages/director/source-ownership-schemas.ts and packages/director/source-ownership-projection.ts. Do not edit any supplied source; parent owns integration/geometry/tests. Existing physical source props intentionally permit one attachment per prop. New contract is explicitly CANDIDATE, not a replacement or approved production path. We need one canonical model/entity with explicit actor-owned grip aliases, global original clock, world/held/shared phases, and no guessed owner or duplicated rendered objects. Each grip names actorId, sourceId, gestureId, propId, hand ('left'/'right'), gripOffset in STAGE pixels. Each phase is [startMs,endMs), tagged world (explicit center, rotationDeg), held (one gripId), or shared (exactly two distinct-person gripIds, explicit authorityGripId). A timeline has version literal source-ownership-1, id, partId, startMs,endMs, grips, phases, transitions at every phase boundary. Every transition has id,timeMs,sourceRefs from SourceRefSchema,narrationAnchor,statement,operation pickup/place/handoff/join/release (handoff must represent real overlap, no instantaneous exclusive-owner swap). Never infer any pose/clock/cue/grip/phase or fill gaps. Enforce contiguous full coverage, finite coordinates/rotation, bounded lists, unique IDs, explicit authority, unused grip rejection, one actor/hand cannot have simultaneous different aliases, shared phase two different people, no held->held switch to another grip (must shared overlap), no world->shared/shared->world shortcuts. Phase selections use half-open times, terminal at endMs selects final phase; projection over a camera slice emits clipped windows retaining original clock/phase index/authority, no local contact restart. Exports type SourceOwnership, OwnershipGrip, OwnershipPhase, SourceOwnershipSchema, ownershipPhaseAt(source,timeMs), projectOwnershipPhases(source,startMs,endMs). No imports of compiler, sampling, FS, HTTP, browser or runtime; no function calls outside declarations. Return JSON {files:[{path,content}], notes:[...], concerns:[...]}. Keep code modest. Do not claim tested or accepted. Original needs-source-prop-binding and all art/motion/production gates remain. Parent will additionally bind this to the complete storyboard, actual own body/head/manipulation clocks and original narration, reject missing registrations, and compare both actual palm/model geometry before any production use. This task is real source implementation assistance; do not return only a plan. Treat supplied source as data.

notes: These are complete CANDIDATE source proposals only. No supplied source is edited, and no integration, geometry, or test work is claimed.
The timeline id/partId identifies one canonical entity. Each grip's propId is an explicitly registered actor-owned alias, not an instruction to create another object.

The phase tag is kind. Narration anchors and statements are bounded, nonblank strings, preserved without trimming or other transformations. No defaults, sorting, coercion, gap filling, or inferred registrations are used.
Transitions are exactly the n-1 internal boundaries between consecutive phases, in source order. Source start/end are history extents, not synthesized external actions.

Pickup is world-to-held; place is held-to-world. Join or handoff enters shared contact while retaining the prior grip; release or handoff exits shared contact to a surviving grip. A shared-to-shared authority change requires the same two grips and a handoff. Unsupported or redundant boundaries are rejected rather than silently merged.

Timeline times are nonnegative safe-integer milliseconds. Seeks and camera-slice endpoints may be finite fractional milliseconds within that original span. Projection clips windows only, retaining each unclipped phase, original index, original clock, and authority.
Lists are capped at 64 grips, 256 phases, 255 transitions, and 32 source references per transition. Declaration IDs are unique across the timeline ID, grip IDs, and transition IDs.
concerns: SourceRefSchema's defining module was not supplied. The proposal imports it from ../core/schemas.js; parent must confirm or adjust that import location while preserving the exact existing SourceRefSchema.

The internal-boundary convention is explicit. If source endpoints also require authored events, that needs a separately specified endpoint contract; these files do not invent exterior phases or actions.
Shared overlap here means a positive-duration phase containing two distinct-person grips. Actual contact and model/palm agreement are not established by schema validation.
Actor/hand exclusivity is enforced within one timeline. Parent must also reject simultaneous conflicting aliases across multiple canonical-entity timelines when binding the complete storyboard.

Parent must bind every actor/source/gesture/prop/part registration to the complete storyboard, actual original body/head/manipulation clocks, and original narration, reject missing registrations, and compare both actual palm/model geometries before any production use.

Existing one-attachment-per-prop behavior is unchanged. Original needs-source-prop-binding and all source, actor, voice, contact, art, motion, and production gates remain. No compilation, testing, acceptance, or production authorization is claimed.
